_description: Material library recipe extracted from /Game/Character_Appearance_Dissolve. Use this to teach ForgePilot how character appearance / dissolve / transformation materials are structured as parent wrappers over reusable Material Functions plus color/intensity instances.
overview: This library is a character-transformation material system, not a set of unrelated one-off shaders. The core pattern is: a parent material supplies a small number of artist-facing parameters and drives a reusable MF_Appearance_* function with a normalized animated Appearance input. Most visual intelligence lives in the material functions. Most parent materials are thin wrappers. Most material instances are just color and emissive variants.
core_library_rules: Inspect the Material Function before judging the parent material. The parent material is usually only a parameter wrapper.
Treat the Appearance input as the main transition driver. It is the dissolve / reveal / transform progress.
Treat Color and Emissive_Mult as style parameters layered on top of a stable transition logic.
Most variants share one of a few structural patterns. Do not think there are 20 fully unique techniques here.
Standard is the authoring/reference source. Mobile is the reduced compatibility branch.

common_structure: Time multiplied by a phase speed
Sine_Remapped used to create an animated 0-1 Appearance driver in some parents
Outputs wired into BaseColor / EmissiveColor / OpacityMask / optional WorldPositionOffset
parent_material_pattern.key_takeaway: ForgePilot should not clone these parents node-for-node. It should understand them as wrappers around reusable transform-function logic.

characteristics: Outputs WPO, Emissive, and Opacity_Mask
Uses texture-driven motion and rotation
Uses bounding-box or object-space driven mapping
Good for transforms that physically peel, swirl, or distort the surface while disappearing
best_for: surface peel or magical skin displacement
animated appearance with visible shape motion

characteristics: Outputs WPO and Emissive, no opacity mask output
Uses SphereMask and world/object position logic
Accepts PointHeight input
Looks suited for reveal waves, point-origin appearance, or vertical/height-driven transform sweeps
best_for: spawn-in effect from a point or height
non-destructive appearance effect where geometry remains but energy travels

characteristics: Outputs Opacity_Mask and Emissive
Uses object local bounds / local-space transforms
Uses texture samples and panners
Uses ceil / saturate / one-minus style threshold shaping
Good for object-space dissolve that respects the mesh volume rather than only UVs
best_for: localized body transform with emissive border

characteristics: Accepts Offset_1 and Offset_2 inputs
Outputs Emissive and Opacity_Mask, and in at least one case Base_Color
Uses sphere or shell-like masking plus offset controls
Good for layered bands, transform shells, or dual-zone appearance transitions
best_for: inner and outer transform shell offsets

characteristics: Simpler node counts
Outputs Opacity_Mask and Emissive
Likely intended as cheaper variants with less support logic
best_for: secondary enemies or cheaper effect tiers
when full hero-function complexity is unnecessary

characteristics: Smallest node counts in the set
Outputs Emissive and Opacity_Mask
Uses panned texture plus bounding-box-based UVW or local-space positioning
Good for cleaner, more graphic edge dissolves and stylized reveal bands

shared_visual_logic: Appearance is the normalized transition amount and should be the primary animation/control input.
Color is a style layer, not the transition logic itself.
Emissive_Mult scales the visual intensity of the reveal edge or energy body.
Object-space or bounding-box-based mapping appears repeatedly because it keeps the dissolve coherent on character forms.
Opacity_Mask is the preferred control for hard reveal/cut transitions in most variants.
WorldPositionOffset is used only in the variants where the transformation needs visible surface displacement or wave motion.
why_this_library_is_valuable: It demonstrates a good separation between reusable material functions and thin parent/instance wrappers.
It treats character transformation as a controlled parameterized system rather than a one-off graph.
It shows several levels of complexity, from hero WPO-driven transforms to compact cheaper dissolve variants.
It is directly relevant to character appearance, corruption, vanish, transform, summon-in, and reveal effects.

recommended_agent_workflow.step_1: Classify whether the requested effect needs WPO, masked dissolve, point/height reveal, shell offset bands, or a compact stylized edge variant.
recommended_agent_workflow.step_2: Choose the closest MF_Appearance_* family, not the closest parent thumbnail.
recommended_agent_workflow.step_3: Expose Appearance as the main driving parameter. Treat it as the effect progress value.
recommended_agent_workflow.step_4: Use Color and Emissive_Mult as material-instance style controls.
recommended_agent_workflow.step_5: Only add Time/Sine_Remapped auto-animation if the effect is ambient or looping. For gameplay-driven transforms, Appearance should usually come from an external parameter.
recommended_agent_workflow.step_6: Use material instances for palette variants instead of duplicating the parent graph.

parameter_mapping_guidance.Appearance: Primary reveal/transform progress. Map from gameplay or sequencer for deterministic character transformation.
parameter_mapping_guidance.Color: Edge or transform energy color. Good candidate for per-variant or per-faction style changes.
parameter_mapping_guidance.Emissive_Mult: Controls strength of the transform edge/glow. Keep this instance-tunable.
parameter_mapping_guidance.PointHeight: Use for vertical sweep or point-origin reveal variants.
parameter_mapping_guidance.Offset_1_and_Offset_2: Use for layered shell widths, dual transform fronts, or inner/outer reveal bands.

if_the_effect_needs.need: surface motion and actual geometric transform feel
reveal from a point or height wave
character dissolve with mesh-coherent object-space breakup

common_failure_modes: Learning from the parent material only and missing the actual logic inside MF_Appearance_*.
Using Time/Sine_Remapped for a gameplay-critical transform that should instead be externally driven.
Duplicating parent materials for color variations instead of using material instances.
Using WPO variants when a simple masked reveal would be clearer and cheaper.
Using a compact stylized variant for a hero transformation that needs volumetric surface motion.
mobile_variant_note: The Mobile folder mirrors the same appearance families in simplified form. Use Standard as the source logic and Mobile only when authoring a mobile-targeted fallback.

agent_recipe.step_1: Resolve the requested character transform into one of the appearance families in this recipe.
agent_recipe.step_2: Use the chosen MF_Appearance_* family as the logic source, not the material instance.
agent_recipe.step_3: Drive Appearance from an external normalized parameter when the transform must sync with gameplay, animation, or sequencer.
agent_recipe.step_4: Keep parent materials thin: BaseColor support, function call, Color, Emissive_Mult, optional WPO and OpacityMask wiring.
agent_recipe.step_5: Spawn Niagara support from the same transform progress if edge particles, sparks, or portal haze are needed.
agent_recipe.step_6: Create style variants through material instances rather than cloning the logic graph.
